checklist: cert/version.mjs: az version is exactly azure-cli <homescoop.upstream>, azure-cli-core and azure-cli-telemetry at the versions of their .dist-info, no extensions, and nothing on stderr; az --version names Python (wasi) 3.15 and the config directory; a first az group list --debug takes upstream's packaged command index (commandIndex.latest.json) and loads only azure.cli.command_modules.resource, with no SyntaxWarning

cert/login.mjs: against a stand-in for Entra ID and ARM behind the kernel's proxy (TLS with the kernel CA): plain az login (can-launch-browser-wasi.patch) and az login --use-device-code print Entra ID's 'open https://login.microsoft.com/device and enter the code' message, never localhost; az asks for the device code with its own client id and the management scope, polls the token endpoint with the device code, lists tenants and subscriptions with the token; az account show, az group list (Bearer token on the ARM call) and az account get-access-token from the cached login; msal_token_cache.json is plain JSON, mode 0600, with the refresh token; az logout empties az account list

cert/sp.mjs: az login --service-principal with a client secret (the client_credentials grant) and with a federated token (client_assertion), az group list with that token, az account get-access-token; service_principal_entries.json mode 0600; a wrong secret is Entra ID's AADSTS7000215 without a traceback

cert/certificate.mjs: az login --service-principal --certificate with a key+certificate PEM made in the kernel with py-cryptography: the client_credentials grant with a client assertion that Node's crypto checks (alg RS256, typ JWT, x5t = the padded base64url SHA-1 of the certificate's DER as pyOpenSSL's digest gives it, no x5t#S256, aud the tenant's token endpoint, iss = sub = the app id, a jti, lifetime <= 1 h, signature verified with the certificate's public key, a changed assertion doesn't verify); az group list (Bearer …-certificate) and az account get-access-token; service_principal_entries.json keeps the certificate's path; a PEM without a certificate is az's 'Invalid certificate, please use a valid PEM file' error, no traceback

cert/keyvault.mjs: az keyvault secret set and show against a stand-in for certvault.vault.azure.net: the SDK's challenge PUT (no token, no body) gets the 401 bearer challenge, az then asks for a client_credentials token for https://vault.azure.net/.default (after the challenge) and sends the PUT again with api-version 7.x, {value, contentType} and that Bearer token (the stand-in takes no other); show reads the value back with a GET /secrets/<name>/ and the same kind of token; az keyvault key import --pem-file (keyvault's custom.py, cryptography at import; 2.93.0-1 stopped here) of an RSA key made in Node sends a PUT /keys/<name> whose JWK n, e, d, p, q, dp, dq and qi are Node's own for that key, and prints n back

cert/sshkeys.mjs: --generate-ssh-keys in az aks create (azure-cli-core's keys.py, cryptography) and az lab vm create (paramiko's RSAKey, with bcrypt and PyNaCl imported): a 2048-bit PEM RSA private key, mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, and an OpenSSH ssh-rsa public key (0644) whose e and n are the private key's (Node's crypto); the managed cluster PUT's linuxProfile.ssh.publicKeys and the lab's createEnvironment sshKey carry it; the two keys differ

cert/webapp.mjs: az webapp list (PyNaCl and fabric at import) against ARM; appservice's _encrypt_github_actions_secret (what az webapp deployment github-actions add sends to GitHub) run in az's process by an extension probe (cert/lib/probe.mjs) seals a publish profile for an X25519 public key made with PyNaCl by a plain python3, which opens both boxes with the private key: the text back, 48 bytes more (crypto_box_SEALBYTES), different each time; another key fails with CryptoError

cert/native.mjs: az keyvault list, az iot hub list, az sf cluster list, az batchai cluster list, az ams content-key-policy list, az webapp list, az functionapp list, az logicapp list and az staticwebapp list exit 0 with [] and no ERROR (each stopped at import in 2.93.0-1); az bot show reaches ARM (Not Found, rc 3); in az's process (extension probe) cryptography and its _rust, _cffi_backend, cffi, pycparser, nacl and its _sodium, bcrypt and OpenSSL come from their /node_modules/@ai-ecoverse/py-* directories, paramiko, fabric, invoke, scp and sshtunnel from lib/azure-cli, lib/azure-cli is first on sys.path and the six py-* site-packages are the only site-packages on it; psutil: az rest --headers key=value --debug exits 0, with the launcher's 'This command needs psutil (native code), which has no WASIX build' line in the debug log and no traceback

cert/storage.mjs: az storage account list (ARM), and az storage blob list, upload and download with an account key against a stand-in for certacct.blob.core.windows.net, every request signed SharedKey; the storage SDKs are unpatched (no homescoop text, module-level from cryptography) and import cryptography from py-cryptography; their client-side encryption ciphers (AES-CBC from blob's and queue's _generate_AES_CBC_cipher, AES-GCM) round-trip

cert/config.mjs: az config get shows core.collect_telemetry=no, core.survey_message=no, extension.use_dynamic_install=no, core.first_run=yes and core.encrypt_token_cache=false from the launcher's environment; bare az shows the welcome without the telemetry notice; no telemetry or az_survey.json files, also in a terminal; az ssh vm (an extension's command) is not found, with no request; az config set survey_message, use_dynamic_install and encrypt_token_cache: the first two win (az_survey.json appears in a terminal), encrypt_token_cache stays false; a caller's environment wins too

cert/launcher.mjs: in wasix-python's site-packages a shadowing yaml (imported at startup by a .pth), a fake cryptography and a fake psutil, and beside az a py-certshadow package (slicc.python.sitePackages, not an az dependency) with a shadow knack and a fake nacl: a plain python3 gets the yaml, cryptography and knack shadows, az gets none (az group list -o yaml, az keyvault list and az webapp list work on az's own tree and py-*, az rest's psutil import is the launcher's error); a py-bcrypt whose package.json says 5.0.0-99 (discovery still gives it to a plain python3) makes az webapp list one ERROR line naming bcrypt, @ai-ecoverse/py-bcrypt, the version found and the 5.0.0-1 az pins; without py-cffi, az keyvault list is one ERROR line: py-cryptography needs py-cffi, which isn't installed (az needs 2.1.1-2); AZURE_CLI_SITEPACKAGES=1 puts site-packages back after az's own (the fake psutil is imported, az's py-cryptography and yaml still win); TLS through the proxy works with CURL_CA_BUNDLE unset (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE from SSL_CERT_FILE); a caller's REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE wins; the launcher under another name exits 1

cert/extension.mjs: az extension add --source of a pure-Python extension wheel made in the kernel installs it with wasix-python's pip into ~/.azure/cliextensions; its command runs, az version lists it, az extension remove takes it out

cert/notices.mjs (homescoop#2112): THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md has a '## <distribution> <version> (<SPDX>)' section with License: and the license text (the notices harness's checkNotices with the built-in phrase; for ANTLR, whose text reads 'Neither name of', that sentence) for each distribution whose wheel ships no license file: antlr4-python3-runtime and isodate (BSD-3-Clause), asn1crypto, wcwidth and the 17 older azure-* packages (MIT), scp (LGPL-2.1-or-later: its LICENSE.txt notice, then the LGPL 2.1 text, paramiko 5.0.0's LICENSE), as licenses.map gives them (read by the spec itself, not meta.json notices: nothing here is linked into a wasm)

test/files.test.mjs (host, the test job): wheels.lock is for the recipe release and the recipe's requirements sha256, and lib/azure-cli has exactly its distributions at its versions; the lock's homescoop lines are exactly the six @ai-ecoverse/py-* dependencies of package.json at their pins, with upstream's own pins recorded, and none of them, nor psutil (the one excluded), is installed or fetched from PyPI; paramiko, fabric, invoke, scp and sshtunnel are; no __pycache__, .pyc, native code, .exe, links or <dist>.data; the packaged command and help index for the release; can-launch-browser-wasi.patch applied and the storage SDKs unpatched; bin/az is src/launcher.py, 0755, the only command; LICENSE is azure-cli's; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md lists every distribution and every license file it names exists

test/launcher.test.mjs (host): src/launcher.py's own_packages() on host python3 against node_modules trees: a flat npm tree and a pnpm store (symlinked entries) give the pinned py-* site-packages in package.json order; another version, a missing package (and its dependent), another ABI, a py-* resolving to another wasix-python, a nested copy of a dependency other than az's, and a python that isn't wasix-python are refused with the reason the ERROR line gives

by hand, not in CI (the cert kernel has no network, CI has no Azure credentials): on slicc-kernel 1.189.2's Node entry with wasm-tls-engine and nodeTransport(), against the real Entra ID: az login --use-device-code and plain az login print a real code for https://login.microsoft.com/device; az --version reached azcliprod.blob.core.windows.net ('Your CLI is up-to-date.'); a service principal login reached the tenant's token endpoint (AADSTS700026 for a made-up app id). The human sign-in with the code was not done

patches.can-launch-browser-wasi.patch: azure-cli-core's can_launch_browser() checks for a browser on WASI as on Linux, so plain az login falls back to the device code flow; without it az says a browser was opened and waits for a localhost redirect (login.mjs times out, NEGATIVE.md)
